headline: 威尼斯影展:鮑伊新片登場
context: 丹尼・鮑伊（Danny Boyle）的新片《Ink》在威尼斯影展登場，講的是梅鐸當年買下《太陽報》、找來雷利・林（Larry Lamb）把它改造成八卦小報霸主的故事。文學評論這邊，文評家泰瑞・伊格頓（Terry Eagleton）83歲推出新書，直面死亡這個他無法迴避的主題；桂冠詩人西蒙・阿米蒂奇（Simon Armitage）則以家鄉哈德斯菲爾德興建墓園為靈感，寫成有聲詩集《New Cemetery》。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Venice film festival Jack O’Connell is terrific as editor Larry Lamb in James Graham’s tale of Rupert Murdoch, Page 3 and the newspaper that transformed Fleet Street Danny Boyle presents us with a lurid, violent and thumpingly unsubtle movie full of Dutch angles, cartoony shocks and gargoyle closeups. It’s a chapter in the prehistory of modern media, adapted by James Graham from his 2017 stage play , filled with shame and fear and self-hate. It is in fact the story of the Sun newspaper, and how Rupert Murdoch (Guy Pearce) bought the ailing minor title in the late 60s and hired a tough Yorkshire newspaperman, Larry Lamb, to turn it into a raucous and gleefully vulgar circulation powerhouse. Ink summons up the energy and frenzy of tabloid papers of the era, but also – and not entirely intentionally – how strangely depressing they were. Audiences used to the super-rich anomie of the Roy family from TV’s Succession might find all this very unsexy. This is a world of officer-class Fleet Street execs having expense-account meals at Rules and the Savoy Grill in pinstripe suits, smoking and drinking and impassively writing salary offers on paper napkins and silently passing them across to each other. Meanwhile, the other ranks of journalists and print unions are covered in sweat and ink. Continue reading...
sources.title: Ink review – Danny Boyle turns the birth of the Sun into a lurid tabloid frenzy

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The literary critic brings his vast reading to bear on life’s most inescapable fact Terry Eagleton is not a fan of sloppy thinking, especially when it comes to the granite fact of death. He particularly doesn’t like the attitude of Dylan Thomas who famously urged his ailing father to “not go gentle into that good night”. If the “night” – death – is so “good” then why, asks Eagleton reasonably, would Thomas want his dad to dawdle? Shouldn’t DJ Thomas, rather, be encouraged to trot towards his lovely end like an ecstatic marathon runner on the home straight? Eagleton’s reproach to Thomas’s doublethink should not be read as panicky denial about the reality of his own mortality. To the contrary, Eagleton, who at 83 admits that he wasn’t sure whether this book would end up being published posthumously, finds it hard to think or write about much else. After a 60-year academic career spent tussling with Marxist literary theory, not to mention the epistemological void at the heart of postmodernism criticism, these days Eagleton is more interested in pondering death and how it “lacks a sense of occasion”. It might visit, for example, while you happen to be dressed in a giraffe outfit. Continue reading...
sources.title: A Death of One’s Own by Terry Eagleton review – meditations on arriving at a full stop

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The building of a cemetery during the pandemic inspires the Huddersfield-born author to reflect on childhood memories and the changing local landscape When Huddersfield council proposed turning some local grazing land into a cemetery during the Covid lockdown, some nearby residents were unhappy. Not poet laureate Simon Armitage, who also lived close to the site. In the introductory essay to his poetry collection, New Cemetery, he notes how the dead would be ideal neighbours for a writer who enjoys quiet. He also “figured that once the departed had taken up residence in the soil, they were unlikely to be evicted to make way for some other form of public amenity or private eyesore”. From his home, Armitage watched as the cemetery took shape, the pastures giving way to walkways, parking bays and neatly arranged burial plots. The verse is rooted in his ruminations around the cemetery’s creation, which coincided with the death of his father who had taught him how to win a fight and the best way to hold an axe (“You’re holding it all wrong / It’s not a pen”). Each poem is named after a species of moth, among them Common Quaker, Dark Brocade, Pine Beauty and May Highflyer, and written in three-line stanzas. Continue reading...
sources.title: New Cemetery by Simon Armitage audiobook review – the poet laureate’s meditations take flight

thread_text:
威尼斯影展:鮑伊新片《Ink》登場。丹尼・鮑伊（Danny Boyle）的新片《Ink》在威尼斯影展登場，講的是梅鐸當年買下《太陽報》、找來雷利・林把它改造成八卦小報霸主的故事。文學這邊，文評家泰瑞・伊格頓（Terry Eagleton）83歲推出新書，直面死亡這個難以迴避的主題；桂冠詩人西蒙・阿米蒂奇（Simon Armitage）則以家鄉哈德斯菲爾德興建墓園為靈感，寫成有聲詩集《New Cemetery》。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 9 月 3 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
threads_text:
丹尼・鮑伊（Danny Boyle）的新片《Ink》在威尼斯影展登場，改編自真實故事，講述媒體大亨梅鐸（Rupert Murdoch）當年買下瀕臨關門的《太陽報》，找來強悍的約克夏報人雷利・林（Larry Lamb），把它改造成八卦小報霸主的過程。文學這邊也有兩則消息：83歲的文評家泰瑞・伊格頓（Terry Eagleton）推出新書，直面死亡這個他坦言難以迴避的主題；桂冠詩人西蒙・阿米蒂奇（Simon Armitage）則以家鄉哈德斯菲爾德在疫情期間興建墓園為靈感，寫成有聲詩集《New Cemetery》。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 9 月 3 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 威尼斯影展上，丹尼・鮑伊有一部新片講的是媒體八卦史。片名叫《Ink》，說的是媒體大亨梅鐸當年買下一家快倒閉的小報，找來一位強悍的報人，把它改造成八卦小報霸主的故事。文學這邊也有兩件事。一位83歲的文評家推出新書，直面死亡這個他說很難迴避的主題。還有一位桂冠詩人，用家鄉在疫情期間興建墓園當靈感，寫成了一本有聲詩集。
